goal: Add a minimal approval-bound HMR loop for evaluating bounded workspace-owned plugin candidates without modifying DSH core or automatically promoting candidates.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Candidate bytes remain inactive until an exact approval is verified, and only fixed files in a verified linked worktree can be published.
Only a successful HMR reload matching the configured entry and candidate digest admits the candidate; failed and unrelated reloads do not.
Failed activation and explicit rejection restore and reactivate the exact snapshotted source bytes.
Run records are evaluation-eligible only for fresh sessions that remain on one admitted HMR generation and include minimal generation provenance.
The coordinator cannot mount itself, edit shared profiles, commit, or promote a candidate; those actions remain human-controlled and separately approved.
The focused HMR proof and complete repository verification gate pass.

outcome.summary: The repository now provides a bounded HMR candidate coordinator, stable-generation run attribution, additive persisted contracts, operator guidance, and passing focused and repository-wide verification.

what_worked: The existing success-only HMR event was sufficient for conservative admission without a DSH core change.
Inactive staging and operation-time approval verification kept denied candidates from publishing live bytes.
Generation sequencing made reload-spanning session attribution fail closed.
An opt-in composition test exercised the coordinator against pinned local Loader, HMR, and Timer artifacts.
what_failed: An initial repository gate found a validation clock older than the updated capsule check date.
The next gate found two dependent capsules whose source digests and claims had not yet been reconciled after documentation changes.
A handoff path label caused a brief false missing-worktree diagnosis; checking the registered repository path confirmed the worktree was intact.

failures_and_inefficiencies.summary: Documentation changes initially left the capsule validation clock and two dependent capsule source bindings stale.
failures_and_inefficiencies.suggested_action: When changing canonical documentation, enumerate every capsule that references each changed source before running the full gate.

failures_and_inefficiencies.summary: An inaccurate path label in the handoff caused an unnecessary recovery detour.
failures_and_inefficiencies.suggested_action: Confirm the repository path through Git before diagnosing a missing temporary worktree.

evidence.summary: DAL-024 defines the bounded HMR candidate loop and its human promotion boundary.
The coordinator implements fixed-path staging, linked-worktree checks, operation-time approval, HMR admission, and rollback.
The recorder binds candidate generation at session creation and derives conservative evaluation eligibility.
The additive run-record contract persists candidate generation and provenance fields.
Focused coordinator, run-recorder, and bundle verification passed with 23 tests and 5 unrelated skips.
The opt-in pinned local DSH Loader, HMR, and Timer composition proof passed without changing DSH source or a shared profile.
The initial full gate failed closed on stale capsule validation metadata; the source bindings and claims were reconciled before retry.
All three committed knowledge capsules validated against their current local sources.
Typecheck, build, 33 test files with 199 passing tests and 7 skips, capsule validation, policy verification, core evaluation, and benchmark evaluation all passed without a hard stop.

uncertainty.statement: A shared-profile or production plugin mount was not exercised because it is a separately approval-gated operation and outside this change's acceptance boundary.
uncertainty.resolution: Obtain an exact unexpired install-or-mount approval for a specific profile before running a separate production integration proof.

notes: No sensitive-action approval was requested or consumed because no shared mount, production candidate application, promotion, or external data transfer occurred.
